title: The Hold Point: Speak-Up Variant
brief: It is 10 a.m. on a Meridian Build site. Slab pour {{lot}} is booked for 11 a.m. and the concrete trucks are on their way. The inspection and test plan has a hold point: the engineer inspects the reinforcement before any pour. A site engineer reports that the section foreman told the crew the inspection will be signed later. This is a 2026 variant on quality culture and speaking up. It is preliminary and excluded from badge scoring and the capstone until verified. You have 12 visit points to gather what you need and make a decision you can justify.

actions.label: Inspection and test plan and pour permit for slab {{lot}}
Rebar delivery tickets and drawing schedule
General condition of the area
actions.note: Nothing of note for the purpose of this visit.

actions.label: Foreman: what was said to the crew
Crew members: what they would do at a hold point that is not signed
Site concern register and a word with the crew

evidence.text: Inspection and test plan ITP-{{lot}}: hold point 4 (reinforcement inspection) is unsigned, yet the pour permit for slab {{lot}} was marked approved by the foreman at 9:40.
evidence.whyItMatters: Work does not pass a hold point until the planned inspection is done and the named person releases it. An approved permit with an unsigned hold point bypasses that. This 2015 requirement is reported to continue in intent; any change in the 2026 wording is unclear.
evidence.missedExplanation: Compare the hold point signatures with the permit status and times.

evidence.text: The rebar delivery tickets for the slab match the bar schedule on drawing S-210 revision D, which is the current revision.
evidence.whyItMatters: The material delivered matches the current drawing, so the inspection can go ahead as planned.
evidence.missedExplanation: Conforming evidence: the data behind the result is sound.
evidence.falseFindingNote: Correct material and current drawing. Conforming.

evidence.text: Section foreman: "The engineer can sign it after. If we send the trucks back we lose the day." The foreman says 2 earlier pours on this project went ahead the same way.
evidence.whyItMatters: The 2026 edition is reported to add a requirement for top management to promote and demonstrate a quality culture and ethical behavior (5.1.1). Pressure from a leader to change a result or skip a check works against it. Acting on a failed check is already a 2015 requirement.
evidence.missedExplanation: Ask the person who applies the pressure what they asked for, and compare it with the release rule.

evidence.text: Crew interviews: 2 of 3 crew members asked did not know they could stop a pour at an unsigned hold point, or whom to call. Site induction record IN-9 covers site rules but not raising quality concerns.
evidence.whyItMatters: Awareness is reported to extend to the organization's quality culture and ethical behavior (7.3). People need to know the route for raising a concern and that they may use it.
evidence.missedExplanation: Ask frontline staff what they would do, and whom they would tell, if a check failed near a deadline.

evidence.text: The site concern register has 0 entries in 12 weeks. Two crew members say a steel fixer who questioned a pour in June was not offered work on the next project.
evidence.whyItMatters: A note on the environment for operation of processes (7.1.4) is reported to recognize that culture can influence operating conditions. Silence after an earlier report was met badly is a sign that the environment discourages reporting. Recorded as an observation because the 2026 wording is unverified.
evidence.missedExplanation: Compare the concern or near-miss log with what staff say in interview. The gap is the evidence.

evidence.text: Nonconformance register: no entry for the 2 earlier pours made before hold point sign-off. The last entry, NCR-52, is 30 days old.
evidence.whyItMatters: Work that passed a hold point without inspection needs a nonconformance record so it can be assessed and its acceptance decided by the engineer. A missing record leaves it unassessed.
evidence.missedExplanation: The procedure names the log. Follow the trail from the procedure to the record.

evidence.text: Procedure QP-08 states that no pour proceeds past a hold point until the engineer signs, and names the project engineer as the person who may release it. The engineer can attend by 12 noon.
evidence.whyItMatters: The organization has a defined route, with named authority, for this exact situation.
evidence.missedExplanation: Conforming evidence: a sound route exists. The risk is in bypassing it.
evidence.falseFindingNote: The procedure is sound and the named person is available. Conforming.

evidence.text: Recognition note RN-14: 4 weeks ago the project manager thanked a labourer at the site briefing for stopping a delivery with the wrong mix ticket. The stop and its outcome are recorded.
evidence.whyItMatters: Thanking a person who stopped work, and recording the outcome, shows leaders supporting the behavior that 5.1.1 is reported to expect.
evidence.missedExplanation: Conforming evidence: a sign of the culture the organization wants.
evidence.falseFindingNote: A recognized stop-work event is good practice, not an issue.

evidence.text: The programme board shows slab {{lot}} booked for 11 a.m.
evidence.whyItMatters: A plan shown on a board is communication, not a nonconformity.
evidence.falseFindingNote: The board shows the plan. A deadline on display is not evidence of a breach.

evidence.text: A daily diary entry has one time struck through with a single line, initialled and dated, with the correct time beside it.
evidence.whyItMatters: A correction that leaves the original legible, with initials and date, protects the integrity of the record.
evidence.falseFindingNote: A single-line correction with initials and date is good record practice. Conforming.

evidence.text: Project review minutes of 2 September list 8 progress and cost measures and no item on concerns raised or how they were handled.
evidence.whyItMatters: Leaders are reported to need to demonstrate a quality culture with evidence (5.1.1). A review meeting is one place to show it. This is an observation, not a nonconformity: commentary says no separate culture program is required, so avoid audit criteria the standard may not state.
evidence.missedExplanation: Read what leaders review. What is never discussed is rarely managed.

decisions.prompt: The trucks arrive in 30 minutes and the foreman wants to pour. What do you do?
options: Let the pour go and ask the engineer to sign later
Ask for the hold point to be kept, call the project engineer now, and ask the supplier whether the delivery can move to just after the noon inspection
Cancel all pours for the week
Say nothing; the foreman runs the section
decisions.rationale: The engineer can inspect by noon, so a short delay keeps the hold point and the day. Speaking up through the named authority is the behavior that 5.1.1 is reported to ask leaders to support.
optionFeedback: This bypasses the hold point and repeats the earlier pattern.
This is proportionate, uses the named authority, and may keep the pour today.
A week-long stop is disproportionate when the engineer is available today.
Staying silent leaves a known bypass unaddressed.

decisions.prompt: The site engineer who raised the concern is new to the project. What should the project manager do?
options: Ask the engineer to deal with such matters quietly in future
Replace the foreman without a review
Do nothing because the pour was delayed
Thank the engineer, confirm that raising it was right, review why hold points were signed late as a system issue, and brief the crews on who may stop a pour
decisions.rationale: Leaders are reported to need to promote and demonstrate a quality culture (5.1.1). Supporting the person who spoke up and fixing the condition, without blame, is the evidence an auditor would look for.

containment: Keep hold point 4 for slab {{lot}} until the engineer has inspected and signed
correction: Have the engineer assess the 2 earlier pours and record the acceptance decision in the nonconformance register
cause: Programme pressure was allowed to override hold points, and crews were not made aware of, or supported in using, the route for raising concerns
corrective: Leaders state and show that hold points are kept; add raising concerns to the site induction; link pour permits to a signed hold point
effectiveness: For the next 10 pours, check that each hold point was signed before the permit and that concerns raised were logged and answered

debriefText.found: You kept the true result, used the defined route, and treated the pressure as a system condition rather than a personal failing.
debriefText.missed: In a culture case, compare what the records say with what people say in interview. Leaders' responses to earlier reports are part of the evidence.
debriefText.falseFinding: A deadline on a board and a properly corrected record are normal. They show planning and good record practice, not a weak culture.

bridge2026.text: Top management is reported to be required to promote and demonstrate a quality culture and ethical behavior. In this case, look at how site leaders respond when a hold point meets a delivery schedule.
Awareness is reported to extend to the organization's quality culture and ethical behavior, so staff should know how to raise a concern and that they may do so.
A note on the environment for operation of processes is reported to recognize that culture and ethical behavior can influence operating conditions.
An auditor checking culture is likely to examine decisions, records of concerns raised, and how leaders responded, rather than attitudes or a separate culture program.
bridge2026.reasoning: Sources describe culture as shown through behavior and evidence, and commentary says no separate culture program is required.
bridge2026.check: Read 5.1.1, its note, and the Annex A guidance on culture in the purchased 2026 text, and ask the certification body how it will audit culture.

bridge2026.text: Release at planned arrangements such as hold points is reported as carried forward in intent from 2015; any change in wording is unclear.
